---
title: "Reported error and reference-law evaluation"
subtitle: "2.9 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 18"
description: "Comparison of conditional error expectations with realised errors at fixed true values."
---

A reported error share is an expectation under the posterior distribution used to select the report. Evaluation
under a separately specified reference law gives another expectation for the same fixed report. The open point
shows the realised share of wrong directions at the simulated league's fixed true values. These quantities need
not coincide. The two lower panels distinguish repeated observation of fixed true values from draws of latent values
conditional on the selected observations. This distinction is necessary when interpreting apparent agreement between
reported and realised error.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Same conditional laws.** The report states 152 pair directions. Both conditional expectations are .0632,
  while the fixed-truth realised share is .0526. Matching expectations does not make a single realization equal
  their common value. Individual repeated datasets give realised shares on either side of this expectation.
- **Narrow prior, five grades.** The report claims .140, while the reference expectation for that same report
  is .115. Their absolute difference is below the largest pair-error gap, .4981. This setting changes the
  prior, cost and grade cap together. Moving just the prior slider also selects a new report; each setting's
  two expectations evaluate that newly selected report under both laws.
- **Lower cost, two grades.** Only 56 pair directions are stated, with claimed share .0254. The two laws still
  agree. In the grade groups, pairs inside a grade are withheld, and the denominator counts only pairs
  stated across grades.
- **One grade, no disclosure.** There are 0 stated directions and every share reads “NA: no disclosure.” No
  wrong directions is different from a defined error share of zero. The posterior-draw wrong count remains
  zero because this report makes no comparisons.

The lower panels separate two experiments. Observation replays keep all true values fixed, redraw estimates,
and choose a new report each time. Posterior draws instead keep the selected observations and report fixed,
then vary latent values under the chosen conditional law. The histogram and running average describe that
chosen law; adding draws reduces simulation noise without testing whether the law is correct.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This is a deterministic teaching league, not true values sampled from the reference prior. Its design scale does
not establish the reference conditional law as the truth. Fixed-truth observation replays therefore do not
instantiate chapter 18's conditional calibration identity. The pair-gap bound compares two model expectations
for one fixed report and does not bound its realised share.
:::

Standalone: [reported and realised shares](../../embed/reported-and-realized.html), for example `?priorSd=.05`.
